subject: EU-only processing & Schrems II: SCCs + retention/deletion Q&A
messages:

Cc: DeltaHealth Legal <legal@deltahealth.de>, procurement@deltahealth.de

Subject: EU-only processing request: Schrems II / SCCs and retention questions

Hi Jonas,

We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot but have firm requirements around EU-only processing because of Schrems II considerations and internal data residency policy. A few specific questions from our security/legal teams: 

- If we choose the hosted API, can you guarantee that all processing (inference + temporary KV/prefix caches + logs/backups) will remain in EU geography only and not transit or land in non-EU regions?
- Are your standard SCCs included in the DPA? We need to understand whether SCCs alone will satisfy our auditors or if we should expect additional contractual safeguards (e.g., technical measures, encryption with BYOK, on-prem options).
- What are your default and minimum retention periods for request logs, audit logs, and KV cache shards? Can deletion be verified and audited?
- For backups and disaster recovery snapshots, where are those stored? Are there subprocessors in the U.S. that will see any customer data?

I've attached a short questionnaire. We're aiming to make a go/no-go decision on a pilot by mid-June. Can we set a 45-minute call next week with your legal and infra folks?

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Müller
Head of Security Programs, DeltaHealth GmbH

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Happy to jump on a call. Quick answers up front so you have context before we schedule: 

- Hosted API can be routed to EU-only regions and we can restrict serving to EU-hosted capacity; however, there are nuances around backups and some global control-plane operations that we should discuss. 
- We include the standard SCCs as part of our DPA; legal has a redline option if additional warranties or SCC clauses are requested. 
- Default logs retention is 30 days for request logs, 90 days for audit logs; we can often shorten request-log retention for enterprise deals (down to 7 days) and provide deletion attestations. 
- Backups are by default stored in EU regions for EU-only customers, but there are historical edge cases where certain snapshot processing touched other regions — we'll confirm and document.

Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Soojin (infra) to provide specifics and a recommended path. If that sounds good, propose Tue/Thu windows next week for a combined legal+tech call.

Best,

Jonas (and team) — high-level legal position and recommended next steps: 

1) SCCs and DPA: We include the EU SCCs in our DPA. For customers with Schrems II concerns we provide an amended DPA that: (a) explicitly lists subprocessors and their regions, (b) adds encryption-at-rest and in-transit commitments, and (c) allows BYOK where feasible. I've attached a redline of the SCCs we prefer to present (SCCs_redline_v2.docx). Key negotiable points: backup residency, access by subprocessors, and data subject rights flow.

2) Technical safeguards to pair with SCCs: BYOK + customer key rotation policy, strict region pinning, logging minimization clauses, and an agreed deletion attestation (we can provide a signed certificate of deletion for the pilot).

3) Residual risk: SCCs alone may not satisfy all auditors if there are US-based subprocessors with access to decrypted data. For a hard requirement of zero non-EU access, recommend Private deployment (VPC or on-prem). 

4) Timeline: If DeltaHealth accepts our redline and agrees to BYOK and a short-term retention window (7 days request logs, 30 days audit logs), legal can turn around a countersigned DPA within ~7 business days.

I'll join the customer call — propose we prepare a concise 1-page security summary and an infra runbook outlining dataflows and control points.

—Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Quick technical summary for the customer-facing doc: 

- Region pinning: We can provision dedicated serving pools in eu-central1 (Frankfurt) or europe-west1 (Belgium) and pin a tenant to those pools. Routing and autoscaling will remain within selected EU regions.
- Caching & KV: KV cache shards are stored in-region and are ephemeral; default TTLs are per-model but we can enforce a strict eviction policy (e.g., no persistent KV beyond request duration) for the pilot.
- Logs & audits: Default request logs 30d / audit 90d. For enterprise deals we can set request logs to 7d and audit logs to 30d via config and provide deletion attestations. Note: some control-plane traces may be routed for telemetry; we can disable non-essential telemetry for this tenant.
- Backups & snapshots: Snapshots are stored in EU regions by default for EU-only customers. We will confirm that our backup provider does not replicate outside EU; if replication exists, we need a contractual carve-out or Private deployment.
- BYOK/KMS: BYOK supported for encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys (Cloud HSM). Key material never leaves customer-managed KMS.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a subprocessors list; most are EU-based for EU-only customers but a few SaaS monitoring tools have limited US processing. For strict EU-only access, Private deployment is the path.

Attachments: I prepared a short infra options PDF and a data flow diagram you can share on the call.

Action items for the call: confirm retention windows, confirm whether BYOK is required, and whether the customer will sign our SCCs redline or needs further concessions.

Thanks,
Soojin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Anna — thanks again for sending this over and for your patience while we pulled the team together. Below is a proposed, practical path forward so you can accelerate the pilot decision: 

Proposed safeguards (pilot):
- Hosting: Tenant pinned to eu-central1 dedicated serving pools.
- Contract: We will present our DPA including SCCs (redline attached).
- Encryption: BYOK (customer-managed KMS) for encryption-at-rest; TLS enforced for all in-flight.
- Retention: Request logs 7 days (for pilot), audit logs 30 days. We will provide a signed deletion attestation after the pilot purge.
- Backups: Stored in EU regions only; we will confirm the backup provider contractually.
- Subprocessors: We will provide a current list and a narrow carve-out for monitoring tools; if DeltaHealth requires zero non-EU subprocessors, recommend Private deployment.

Mutual Action Plan (high-level) — target: pilot start in ~4 weeks if all OK
1) This week: customer to confirm BYOK requirement and required retention windows.
2) +3 business days: Redwood legal sends DPA redline (attached) for review.
3) +7 business days after agreement: infra onboarding (provision EU dedicated pool, configure BYOK, retention policies).
4) Pilot: 2–4 week pilot with deletion attestation at end.

Next steps: 
- Please confirm whether DeltaHealth requires BYOK and whether the retention windows above are acceptable.
- I propose a joint call next Tue (2026-06-09) for 45 minutes — Kimberly and Soojin will join.
